title: Agentic-OPD: Recovering Forgotten Agent Capabilities via On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Tasks
trick: Keep every checkpoint of a GRPO run, mark which validation problems each one solves, then distill into the best checkpoint from whichever old checkpoint covers most of its current failures, only on failed rollouts.
framing_stripped: Called 'recovering forgotten agent capabilities', 'temporal checkpoint consolidation as weak-to-strong OPD' with an 'HCN policy' and a 'LAD module'; it is (a) a count, per saved checkpoint of one GRPO run, of which validation problems a single greedy decode gets right, showing the union over checkpoints is far larger than any one checkpoint's set (sec. 2, Figure 1, App. A.2); and (b) a post-RL fine-tuning stage that continues training the best-validation checkpoint on the same training data by reverse-KL on its own rollouts toward a frozen earlier checkpoint, where the teacher is re-chosen every $K$ steps as the one whose greedy-solved set most covers the student's current validation failures (weighted set cover, eqs. 6-9), and the loss is restricted to problems where the teacher's sampled success rate beats the student's, to the student's failed rollouts on them, and to student-generated tokens (eqs. 10-13); gains of +2.8 / +7.4 / +2.6 exact-match points on DeepSearch for Qwen2.5-3B / 7B / Qwen3-4B (Table 1) and +0.4 to +6.0 on four other domains at 3B (Tables 4-7).
method_equations: Outcome indicator (sec. 2, eq. 1): for task $x$ with reference answer $y^{*}(x)$ and a policy $\pi$ whose multi-turn episode ends in final answer $\hat{y}_{\pi}(x)$, $$C_{\pi}(x) = \mathbf{1}\bigl[\hat{y}_{\pi}(x) = y^{*}(x)\bigr],$$ with the environment's own success predicate substituted where the outcome is not an answer string; $r(x, \hat{y}) \in \{0, 1\}$ is the same indicator applied to one rollout answer $\hat{y}$ (sec. 3.1). How 'solved' is decided: one deterministic draw per (checkpoint, problem): 'We use greedy decoding for all checkpoint evaluations' (sec. 2); no pass@k, no repeated samples, no temperature in the forgetting measurement. Checkpoints: the detailed case trains Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct with GRPO on HotpotQA only for 500 steps, saving and evaluating a checkpoint every 5 steps, $n = 100$ checkpoints, on $\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{val}}$ = a random 10% split of the training queries (size not stated; at least 4,553 from the counts below); the other four domains evaluate every saved checkpoint (default interval 10 RL steps, sec. 3.1; count not stated) on the domain validation set, step 0 excluded (App. A.2). Solved set, $k$-fold union and gap (eqs. 2-3), with $T_i$ the $i$-th saved checkpoint and $d$ the domain: $$Q_i^{(d)} = \bigl\{x \in \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{val}}^{(d)} : C_{T_i}(x) = 1\bigr\}, \qquad U_{\geq k}^{(d)}(i) = \Bigl\{x \in \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{val}}^{(d)} : \sum_{j=1}^{i} \mathbf{1}\bigl[x \in Q_j^{(d)}\bigr] \geq k\Bigr\}, \qquad G_i^{(d)} = \bigl|U_{\geq 1}^{(d)}(i) \setminus Q_i^{(d)}\bigr|,$$ so $U_{\geq 1}^{(d)}(i)$ is the historical union through checkpoint $i$ and $G_i^{(d)}$ counts problems some earlier checkpoint solved and $T_i$ does not; 'Raising $k$ drops the tasks only a single checkpoint ever solved' (sec. 2). Union-vs-best numbers: at step 500 'the final checkpoint solves 2,808 tasks, while 4,553 tasks are solved by at least three checkpoints, a difference of 62%' (sec. 2; note this compares the final checkpoint, not the best-validation one, against $U_{\geq 3}$); the per-domain best-checkpoint-vs-$U_{\geq 1}$ relative gaps are annotated only in Figure 1(b) and the per-domain curves only in Figure 5 (numbers not in text); App. A.2: 'The gap is present in every domain and does not close with training. It is widest on ReTool and WebShop ... and narrowest on SciWorld, where both curves saturate near the size of the validation set'. Recovery accounting (sec. 4.3, Qwen3-4B, 2,000 routing-validation questions, 1,000 each from NQ and HotpotQA, 100 teachers saved every 5 steps through step 500, student at OPD update 20 chosen on the same set): the student 'recovers 60 questions from the historical union while losing 45 previously solved questions, for a net gain of 15 questions (+0.75 percentage points, from 55.25% to 56.0%)'; unweighted coverage of teacher $i$ is $100 \, |Q_i \setminus P_{20}| / 2{,}000$; the most accurate teacher (step 490, 54.9%) covers 57 remaining failures (2.85 points), the most complementary (step 250, 52.75%) covers 78 (3.9 points). HCN (sec. 3.2, eqs. 4-9): scheduling steps $t$ occur every $K$ training steps; $\pi_{S,t}$ is the student at stage $t$; each candidate's solved set is recorded once and the student's refreshed at every stage, $$Q_i = \{x \in \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{val}} : C_{T_i}(x) = 1\}, \quad P_t = \{x \in \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{val}} : C_{\pi_{S,t}}(x) = 1\}, \quad \Delta_{i,t} = Q_i \setminus P_t,$$ where $\Delta_{i,t}$ is the gain set of candidate $i$ (rows of the gain matrix). Each problem carries a priority weight $w_t(x)$, $w_0(x) = 1$; weighted coverage $g_{i,t} = \sum_{x \in \Delta_{i,t}} w_t(x)$ (eq. 7); after a stage with activated teacher index $i_t^{*}$, $$w_{t+1}(x) = \begin{cases} 0, & x \in P_{t+1}, \\ 1, & x \in Q_{i_t^{*}} \setminus P_{t+1}, \\ \min\{w_t(x) + \eta, \, w_{\max}\}, & \text{otherwise}, \end{cases}$$ with increment $\eta > 0$ and cap $w_{\max}$ (eq. 8): solved problems get zero weight, unsolved problems the current teacher covered return to 1, unsolved problems nobody covered gain priority. Selection (eq. 9): $$T_t^{*} = T_{i_t^{*}}, \qquad i_t^{*} = \arg\max_{i \in \mathcal{C}_t} g_{i,t}, \qquad \mathcal{C}_t = \{i \in [n] : g_{i,t} > 0\},$$ ties to the earlier checkpoint; the teacher supervises the next $K$ steps, then $P_{t+1}$ is refreshed; consolidation stops when $\mathcal{C}_t = \emptyset$. Values of $K$, $\eta$, $w_{\max}$: unknown (not in text). LAD (sec. 3.3, eqs. 10-12): for a training problem $x \in \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{train}}$ the student $S$ and the activated teacher $T_t^{*}$ each draw $G$ rollouts with answers $\hat{y}^{(j)}_S$, $\hat{y}^{(j)}_{T_t^{*}}$, $$s(x) = \frac{1}{G} \sum_{j=1}^{G} r\bigl(x, \hat{y}_S^{(j)}\bigr), \qquad q_t(x) = \frac{1}{G} \sum_{j=1}^{G} r\bigl(x, \hat{y}_{T_t^{*}}^{(j)}\bigr),$$ problem filter $\mathcal{X}_t = \{x : q_t(x) > s(x)\}$ (eq. 11; drops problems where both rates are zero), rollout filter $\mathcal{F}(x) = \{j \in [G] : r(x, \hat{y}_S^{(j)}) = 0\}$ for $x \in \mathcal{X}_t$ (eq. 12), so the teacher's rollouts only estimate $q_t(x)$ and distillation runs on the student's failed trajectories; $G$: unknown (not in text). So the selection sets $Q_i, P_t$ are greedy single decodes on $\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{val}}$ while the LAD rates $s, q_t$ are $G$-sample success rates on $\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{train}}$. OPD loss (eq. 13): for a retained trajectory $\tau$, $\mathcal{G}(\tau)$ is the set of student-generated token positions (think, action, answer turns; prompt, observations, tool returns and padding excluded); at position $\ell$ with prefix $\tau_{<\ell}$, $A_\ell^{(k)}$ is the student's top-$k$ token set and both policies are renormalised on it, $p^{(k)}_{\pi}(v \mid \tau_{<\ell}) = \pi(v \mid \tau_{<\ell}) / \sum_{u \in A_\ell^{(k)}} \pi(u \mid \tau_{<\ell})$; $$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{OPD}} = \frac{1}{\sum_{\tau} |\mathcal{G}(\tau)|} \sum_{\tau} \sum_{\ell \in \mathcal{G}(\tau)} D_{\mathrm{KL}}\Bigl(p^{(k)}_{S,t}(\cdot \mid \tau_{<\ell}) \,\Big\|\, p^{(k)}_{T_t^{*}}(\cdot \mid \tau_{<\ell})\Bigr),$$ a reverse KL (student first) computed from one frozen-teacher forward pass per retained trajectory; $k$: unknown (not in text). Consolidation loop (sec. 3.4, App. A.3): DAPO-style oversampling, draw batches of $B$ problems until the sequences retained by eqs. 11-12 fill one batch of $B_{\mathrm{eff}} = BG$ sequences, at most $L$ draws; if a fraction $\rho$ of student rollouts survives the filters, filling a batch costs about $B / \rho$ problems and $2BG / \rho$ rollouts split between student and teacher, plus the teacher forward passes and the periodic evaluation of pool and student on $\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{val}}$; $B$, $L$, $\rho$: unknown (not in text). Noise control on the forgetting measurement: none run; no checkpoint is decoded twice, no per-problem success probability is estimated for $Q_i$, and the only robustness device is $U_{\geq 2}$, $U_{\geq 3}$; paired bootstrap 95% CIs over task instances and three seeds are mentioned only for SciWorld checkpoint comparisons (App. A.2). Observed consolidation results (Table 1, exact match %, mean of seven DeepSearch benchmarks): Qwen2.5-3B GRPO 35.6 vs Agentic-OPD 38.4; Qwen2.5-7B 38.8 vs 46.2; Qwen3-4B 47.8 vs 50.4; OPSD 25.1 / 29.9 / 28.7 against base 26.0 / 29.6 / 28.0. Table 2 (3B, NQ / HotpotQA): GRPO 42.1 / 34.8; uniform soup 42.5 / 35.1; greedy soup 43.4 / 35.9; TIES 43.0 / 35.6; DARE-TIES 43.7 / 36.2; EMA 42.8 / 35.5; GTR-Turbo (merging plus RL) 45.0 / 37.4; Temporal Sampling (inference ensemble) 44.6 / 37.1; Agentic-OPD 45.4 / 37.9; w/o HCN (uniform teacher sampling) 43.6 / 36.1; w/o LAD 42.7 / 35.3. Other domains at 3B (Tables 4-7, GRPO vs Agentic-OPD): Tool-use mean pass@1 26.1 vs 32.1 (32 repeats, temperature 1.0, top-$p$ 0.7); SciWorld Overall 14.4 vs 18.0; WebShop mean of score and success 71.8 vs 75.0; ALFWorld All 88.5 vs 91.0 with Heat falling 96.0 to 92.0.
load_bearing_assumption: That a problem in $U_{\geq 1} \setminus Q_{\mathrm{best}}$ is a capability the run had and the best checkpoint lost, rather than a problem the policy solves with probability near one half whose single greedy decode happened to land on the right side at some checkpoint. Everything rests on $C_{T_i}(x)$ being one greedy decode per checkpoint ('We use greedy decoding for all checkpoint evaluations', sec. 2): under tiny parameter changes (5 RL steps) a greedy argmax at a near-tied token flips, so a problem whose success probability sits at 0.5 under sampling will enter $U_{\geq 1}$ within a few checkpoints and appear 'forgotten' at every checkpoint where the argmax falls the other way; with $n = 100$ checkpoints, $U_{\geq 3}$ (4,553) is still reachable by such coin-flip problems, and the paper's own best-case recovery (60 recovered, 45 lost, net 15 of 2,000, sec. 4.3) is the size of churn a knife-edge account would predict. The paper does not estimate per-problem success probabilities for any checkpoint on $\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{val}}$, does not re-decode one checkpoint under sampling to get the noise floor, and never reports how many problems in the gap set a fixed checkpoint solves with probability above, say, 0.8 at an earlier step and below 0.2 at the best step (the only reading of 'forgotten' that is a property of the policy). Second, that the test-set gains come from the teachers rather than from more training on $\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{train}}$: 'RL and OPD use the same training data' (sec. 4.1), the student keeps sampling $G$ rollouts per problem and updating, and no arm continues GRPO (or self-distills from the student's own successful rollouts with the same LAD filters) for the same number of updates and tokens; the closest control, GTR-Turbo with 'additional RL updates', lands within 0.4 / 0.5 points (Table 2).
weakest_component: For this lane, the forgetting ruler: 'solved' is one greedy decode per (checkpoint, problem), so the union-vs-best gap is measured without a noise floor; the 62% headline (sec. 2) is $U_{\geq 3}$ (4,553) over the final checkpoint (2,808), not the best-validation checkpoint the abstract names; the per-domain relative gaps are only annotated in Figure 1(b) and never tabulated; and the SciWorld curves are conceded to have 'low statistical power' (App. A.2). Then, in order: (1) no compute-matched control: the OPD stage is extra training on the RL training set with teacher-side rollouts costing $2BG / \rho$ per batch (App. A.3), and no 'continue GRPO for the same budget' or 'self-distill from own successes with LAD' arm exists; the ablation 'w/o HCN' (uniform teacher sampling) keeps +1.5 / +1.3 points and 'w/o LAD' keeps +0.6 / +0.5 (Table 2), so how much of the +3.3 / +3.1 is the scheduler, the filter, or simply more steps is not separable. (2) The validation set does double duty: $\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{val}}$ selects teachers (eq. 9), the student checkpoint is picked on it, and the recovery analysis is run on it, which the paper concedes 'describes consolidation behavior rather than independent test-set performance' (sec. 4.3); the measured net recovery there is +0.75 points while the Qwen3-4B test gain is +2.6 (Table 1), so the recovery mechanism accounts for less than a third of the reported gain on the only set where it is measured. (3) The abstract on the arXiv listing says the 4B student surpasses 'GPT-5.6 and DeepSeek-V4.1 on deep search' while the body says the reference scores 'reflect fit to the protocol rather than general capability. We include them as context and do not rank Agentic-OPD against them' (sec. 4.2): the reference models are run with a four-turn limit and exact match without training on the protocol. (4) The 7B gain (+7.4) is three times the 3B and 4B gains (+2.8, +2.6) on a GRPO baseline (38.8) that is 9 points below the 4B GRPO baseline (47.8); one backbone drives the headline number. (5) Hyperparameters $K$, $\eta$, $w_{\max}$, $G$, $k$, $B$, $L$, the number of OPD updates, GPU-hours, and confidence intervals for Tables 1-2 are not in the text; DeepSearch results are single runs with no seed count stated (three seeds only for WebShop, SciWorld, ALFWorld, App. A.1).
regime: Models: Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct (all five domains, all ablations and merging baselines), Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 (DeepSearch only). RL: GRPO with verifiable outcome rewards, following Search-R1 (DeepSearch, Wikipedia retriever, 4 turns), ReTool (Tool-use, Python interpreter, 16 turns), AgentGym-RL (WebShop 20 turns, SciWorld 15, ALFWorld 50) (App. A.1, Table 3). Checkpoints: saved every 10 RL steps by default; the preliminary DeepSearch run saves every 5 steps for 500 steps ($n = 100$); counts for the other domains not stated. Validation: 10% of NQ and HotpotQA train for teacher selection; a separate HotpotQA-only run for the preliminary study; 2,000 routing-validation questions for the sec. 4.3 analysis. Evaluation: greedy decoding for every checkpoint in the forgetting measurement; Tool-use pass@1 as the mean of 32 repeats at temperature 1.0, top-$p$ 0.7; AgentGym domains at temperature 0.7, top-$p$ 0.8, top-$k$ 20, three seeds; DeepSearch exact match on NQ, HotpotQA (in-domain), PopQA, TriviaQA, 2Wiki, MuSiQue, Bamboogle (out-of-domain). Pass bands: DeepSearch mean EM 35.6-50.4 after RL/OPD; Tool-use mean pass@1 26.1-32.1 with AIME 2024/2025 at 7.9-15.5; ALFWorld 88.5-91.0 (near ceiling); SciWorld Overall 14.4-18.0; WebShop success 63-66. Compute: 'All training runs use one node with 8 $\times$ A800 80GB GPUs' (sec. 4.1); GPU-hours, OPD update count, and dollar cost: unknown (not in text). Date: arXiv 2026-11-09 (v1 listing); venue not stated.
information_asymmetry: (1) Selection time vs run time. Best-validation selection reads one scalar per checkpoint and discards the per-problem vector $C_{T_i}(x)$ behind it; a richer version exists in the GRPO rollouts themselves, since every training step already scores $G$ sampled rollouts per problem with $r(x, \hat{y})$, so a per-problem success-probability trajectory $\hat{p}_i(x) = \frac{1}{G}\sum_j r(x, \hat{y}^{(j)}_{T_i})$ over steps is computed and thrown away. The paper rebuilds a coarse version after the fact on $\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{val}}$ by one greedy decode per checkpoint (eqs. 2-4); the LAD filter uses $G$-sample rates (eq. 10) only on $\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{train}}$ and only to admit problems, never to define forgetting. (2) What the solved sets contain. $Q_i$ holds the problems whose greedy argmax path, through a deterministic retriever or sandbox over 4-50 turns, ended in the reference string; it mixes problems solved with probability near 1, knife-edge problems near 0.5 whose greedy decode flips under 5-step parameter changes, and retrieval accidents. A 'forgotten problem' ($x \in U_{\geq 1} \setminus Q_{\mathrm{best}}$) is therefore a probability drop or an argmax flip, and the paper cannot tell which; the separating control, decoding a few checkpoints $m$ times at the RL sampling temperature and counting gap problems that move by more than the within-checkpoint binomial spread, costs a few hundred GPU-hours at 3B and is not run. (3) Where the ideas are. The lane result would be a per-problem probability trajectory with a noise floor: how much of $G_i$ survives at $\hat{p} > 0.8 \to \hat{p} < 0.2$, whether it concentrates in a problem type or step range, and whether the union-vs-best gap exceeds the gap between two independent samples of one checkpoint. The same record would let HCN schedule by expected gain rather than greedy set cover, and would price the recipe: +0.75 points net recovery (sec. 4.3) against $2BG / \rho$ rollouts per batch (App. A.3).
occupies: Published: the observation, on five agentic domains trained with GRPO from Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, that the per-checkpoint greedy-solved validation sets have a union far larger than any single checkpoint's set (final checkpoint 2,808 vs 4,553 solved by at least three of 100 checkpoints on HotpotQA; gap present and non-closing in every domain, Figure 1 and 5); the recipe that treats all saved checkpoints as frozen teachers and the best-validation checkpoint as student, picks the teacher by priority-weighted set cover of the student's current validation failures (HCN, eqs. 6-9), restricts top-$k$-renormalised reverse-KL distillation to problems where the teacher's $G$-sample success rate beats the student's, to failed student rollouts, and to student tokens (LAD, eqs. 10-13), with DAPO-style oversampling to fill batches; gains of +2.8 / +7.4 / +2.6 DeepSearch EM on Qwen2.5-3B / 7B / Qwen3-4B and improvements in Tool-use, WebShop, SciWorld, ALFWorld at 3B; the comparison on NQ/HotpotQA against model soups, TIES, DARE-TIES, checkpoint EMA, GTR-Turbo and Temporal Sampling from the same run; the ablations w/o HCN and w/o LAD; and the recovery accounting (60 recovered, 45 lost at the best OPD validation checkpoint). Not claimed and left open: any noise floor for the forgetting measurement (per-problem success probabilities, repeated decodes, a two-sample control on one checkpoint); the best-validation (rather than final) checkpoint against the union in text; a compute-matched continued-GRPO or self-distillation arm; recovery measured on a held-out set; models above 7B; non-Qwen backbones; the stated hyperparameters.

neighbors.title: Temporal Sampling for Forgotten Reasoning in LLMs
neighbors.trick: Show that SFT and RL fine-tuning make a model stop solving problems it previously got right ('temporal forgetting'), and at test time draw samples from several checkpoints along the run instead of one, recovering 4-19 Pass@k points without retraining; this paper takes the phenomenon from there (Temporal Forgetting Scores of 6.4% to 56.1% in CoT math, sec. 2), asks whether it holds for multi-turn agents, and replaces the inference-time ensemble with a single distilled student, beating Temporal Sampling by 0.8 points on NQ and HotpotQA (Table 2).

neighbors.title: GTR-Turbo: Merged Checkpoint is Secretly a Free Teacher for Agentic VLM Training
neighbors.trick: Merge the weights of the checkpoints an RL run has produced so far and use the merged model as a free step-level teacher for the ongoing RL via SFT or soft logit distillation, replacing a privileged VLM teacher; this paper keeps the checkpoints separate instead of merging ('Parameter-space merging ... can erase checkpoint-specific strengths', sec. 1) and reports GTR-Turbo as its strongest baseline, within 0.4 / 0.5 points on NQ / HotpotQA (Table 2).

neighbors.title: Self-Distilled Reasoner: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Large Language Models
neighbors.trick: Let one model be both teacher and student: the teacher context includes privileged information such as a verified reasoning trace, the student sees only the question, and training minimises the per-token divergence between the two on the student's own rollouts; here OPSD is the single-model OPD baseline and stays within one point of the base model on every DeepSearch backbone (Table 1), which the paper reads as 'privileged information for a teacher using the same model as the student is insufficient' in agentic tasks (sec. 4.2).

neighbors.title: MOPD: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Capability Integration in LLM Post-Training
neighbors.trick: Run per-domain RL to get one specialist teacher per capability, then distill all of them into one student on the student's own rollouts, so capabilities developed in parallel are merged without Mix-RL or weight merging (deployed in MiMo-V2-Flash); this paper positions its teachers as temporal checkpoints of one run rather than parallel specialists ('Most use parallel or independently developed teachers', sec. 6.1) and adds a selection rule and a locality filter because each teacher is globally weaker than the student.

neighbors.title: Counteraction-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for General Capability Recovery with Domain Preservation
neighbors.trick: When a domain-specialised model has lost general ability, alternate dedicated recovery updates from a general teacher with periodic domain-preservation updates, and keep only samples with large averaged token-level teacher-student log-probability gaps, to stop recovery and preservation gradients cancelling; this paper cites it among multi-teacher OPD methods for 'capability integration and conflicts' (sec. 6.1) and shares its gap-based sample selection idea, applied here at the problem and rollout level with outcome rewards instead of log-probability gaps.

theme_fit.why: forgetting and transfer inside one long-horizon agent RL run, measured across checkpoints on five multi-turn domains (4-50 turns), is a lane-sentence question; the measurement is what the lane watches and it is left without a noise floor (one greedy decode per checkpoint, no repeated-sampling control, final rather than best-validation checkpoint in the 62% headline), which is a definitive-comparison shape under one GPU-week at 3B; the recipe half (HCN plus LAD on the same benchmarks, no compute-matched arm) is the lane's out-of-scope 'new recipe' and is lab-contested

supplies an instrument, the per-checkpoint solved set and its union-vs-best gap, whose validity turns on exactly the lane's reliability question: whether 'solved' from a single draw is a property of the policy or of the draw (pass^k across versions, here versions are checkpoints 5 steps apart); also an evaluation-protocol flag, frontier reference models scored under a 4-turn exact-match protocol they were not trained for and the listing abstract ranking against them while the body declines to

the consolidation loop's cost is written down as $2BG / \rho$ rollouts per batch plus pool evaluation (App. A.3) but never measured in GPU-hours or dollars; same words (rollout cost), different problem

limitations_as_complaints: I call a problem 'forgotten' when one greedy decode of an earlier checkpoint got it right and one greedy decode of the best checkpoint got it wrong, and I never check whether a single checkpoint sampled twice would show the same churn: 'We use greedy decoding for all checkpoint evaluations' (sec. 2); my only robustness device is counting problems 'solved by at least $k$ of the checkpoints' with 'Raising $k$ drops the tasks only a single checkpoint ever solved' (sec. 2), and I concede that 'measuring how much of the historical task coverage can be reliably recovered' is still a 'useful next step' (sec. 5) [paraphrase: no per-problem success probability, no repeated-decode noise floor, no CIs on the 2,808-vs-4,553 gap are in the text; bootstrap CIs are mentioned only for SciWorld, App. A.2].

My recovery is small, leaky, and measured on the set I select on: 'The student recovers 60 questions from the historical union while losing 45 previously solved questions, for a net gain of 15 questions (+0.75 percentage points, from 55.25% to 56.0%)' and 'substantial losses remain even at the best observed validation checkpoint' (sec. 4.3); 'Since this checkpoint is selected on the same validation set, the analysis describes consolidation behavior rather than independent test-set performance' (sec. 4.3); 'Recovery remains incomplete, however, and some tasks show regressions' (sec. 5), e.g. ALFWorld Heat 96.0 to 92.0 (App. A.4).

My stage costs extra rollouts and evaluations that I never price or match against simply training longer: 'filling the batch requires approximately $B / \rho$ sampled problems and $2BG / \rho$ rollouts, split evenly between the student and the activated teacher' plus a teacher forward pass per retained trajectory and 'evaluating the frozen teacher pool on the validation set and periodically re-evaluating the student' (App. A.3); 'Consolidation also requires additional sampling and evaluation ... Reducing this cost ... [is a] useful next step' (sec. 5) [paraphrase: no GPU-hour figure, no continued-GRPO or self-distillation arm at equal compute; GTR-Turbo with extra RL updates lands within 0.4 / 0.5 points, Table 2].
